([[Branson, Missouri]]) | college = * [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]] (2022–2024) * [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn]] (2024–2026) | highlights = * First-team [[List of All-Big East Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big East]] (2026) * [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Sixth Man of the Year|Big East Sixth Man of the Year]] (2025) }} '''Tarris A. Reed Jr.''' (born August 5, 2003) is an American [[college basketball]] player for the [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn Huskies]] of the [[Big East Conference]]. He previously played for the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]]. ==Early life and high school== For his first three years of high school, Reed went to [[Chaminade College Preparatory School (Missouri)|Chaminade College Preparatory School]] in [[St. Louis, Missouri]]. In his senior year he went to [[Link Academy (Missouri)|Link Academy]] in [[Branson, Missouri]].{{cite web |title=2025-26 Men's Basketball Roster, Tarris Reed Jr. |url=https://uconnhuskies.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/tarris-reed-jr-/14930 |website=uconnhuskies.com |date=28 October 2020 |access-date=27 March 2026}} As a sophomore, Reed averaged 14.5 points and 8.5 rebounds per game.{{cite web |last1=Wallace |first1=Dylan |title=Indiana Basketball Offers 2022 Four-Star Forward Tarris Reed Jr. |url=https://www.si.com/college/indiana/recruiting/indiana-basketball-offers-2022-four-star-forward-tarris-reed-jr |work=Indiana Hoosiers on SI |publisher=SI.com |date=28 October 2020 |access-date=3 April 2024}} As a junior, he averaged 21.8 points, 11.5 rebounds, 1.4 assists, and 2.6 blocks per game, earning him 2021 [[Greater St. Louis]] Player of the Year recognition from the ''[[St. Louis Post-Dispatch]]'' and ''[[The St. Louis American]]''.{{cite web|url=https://www.stlamerican.com/sports/sports-columnists/inside-sports/st-louis-americans-fab-five-boys-basketball-team/|title=St. Louis American’s “Fab Five” boys basketball team|accessdate=January 13, 2025|date=April 16, 2021|work=[[The St. Louis American]]|author=Austin Jr., Earl}}{{cite web|url=https://www.stltoday.com/sports/high-school/all-metro/boys-basketball/all-metro-boys-basketball-player-of-the-year-reed-is-the-next-great-red-devil/article_c3e6907c-93d6-11eb-8e4c-abbccae662b4.html|title=All-Metro boys basketball player of the year: Reed is the next great Red Devil|accessdate=January 13, 2025|date=April 3, 2021|work=[[St. Louis Post-Dispatch]]|author=Kvidhal, David|url-access=subscription}} Coming out of high school, Reed was rated a four-star recruit, the 13th ranked center, and the 69th overall player in the class of 2022.{{cite web |last1=Kahn |first1=Andrew |title=Scouting report on Michigan basketball commit Tarris Reed Jr. |url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/2021/08/scouting-report-on-michigan-basketball-commit-tarris-reed-jr.html |website=MLive.com |access-date=4 April 2024}} Reed committed to play [[college basketball]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]] over offers from school such as [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]], [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]], [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]], [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]], [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]], [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]] and [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]].{{cite web |last1=Sang |first1=Orion |title=Michigan basketball adds 4-star center Tarris Reed to 2022 recruiting class |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2021/08/05/michigan-basketball-recruiting-center-tarris-reed-commitment/5502860001/ |website=Detroit Free Press |access-date=4 April 2024}} ==College career== ===Michigan=== Reed enrolled at the [[University of Michigan]] in 2022. He played sparingly his freshman season, but as a sophomore, Reed started 31 of 32 games, averaging 9.0 points per game, a team-high 7.2 rebounds per game, and 1.4 blocks per game on 51.9 percent shooting.{{cite web |last1=Hawkins |first1=James |title=Michigan basketball loses another starter to the transfer portal |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/2024/03/19/tarris-reed-jr-latest-michigan-wolverines-basketball-player-to-enter-transfer-portal/73028666007/ |website=The Detroit News |access-date=3 April 2024}} He tallied 19 points, six rebounds and three blocks in a win over [[2023-24 Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball team|Iowa]] on December 10, 2023.{{cite web |last1=Kahn |first1=Andrew |title=Michigan, Tarris Reed Jr. have much-needed breakout game at Iowa |url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/2023/12/michigan-tarris-reed-jr-have-much-needed-breakout-game-at-iowa.html |website=MLive.com |date=11 December 2023 |access-date=3 April 2024}} On January 4, 2024, Reed recorded his first career double-double versus [[2023-24 Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball team|Minnesota]], scoring 14 points and bringing down 11 rebounds.{{cite web |last1=Garcia |first1=Tony |title=Michigan basketball loses another as center Tarris Reed Jr. enters transfer portal |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2024/03/19/michigan-basketball-tarris-reed-jr-ncaa-transfer-portal-juwan-howard/73028208007/ |website=Detroit Free Press |date=19 March 2024 |access-date=3 April 2024}} On January 18, he posted a career-high 20 points against [[2023-24 Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball team|Illinois]].{{cite web |last1=Rutter |first1=Eric |title=Tarris Reed Jr. Hits Transfer Portal |url=https://www.si.com/college/michigan/basketball/tarris-reed-transfer-portal-michigan-basketball |work=Michigan Wolverines on SI |publisher=SI.com |date=19 March 2024 |access-date=3 April 2024}} After the season, he entered the [[NCAA transfer portal]]. ===UConn=== Reed transferred to UConn in the spring of 2024. He received the [[Big East Conference]] [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Sixth Man of the Year|Sixth Man of the Year]] award in 2025.{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/awards/men/big-east-sixth-man.html |title=Men's Big East Conference Sixth Man of the Year Winners |website=[[Sports Reference]]|accessdate=April 24, 2025}} Following the 2025–26 regular season, he was named first-team All-[[2025–26 Big East Conference men's basketball season|Big East]], marking the first trio of first-team selections in the Big East from one team. He joined [[2025–26 UConn Huskies men's basketball team|UConn]] teammates, [[Silas Demary Jr.]] and [[Alex Karaban]].{{cite web|url=https://www.bigeast.com/news/2026/3/8/mens-basketball-2025-26-all-big-east-teams-announced.aspx|title=2025-26 All-BIG EAST Teams Announced|accessdate=March 10, 2026|date=March 8, 2026|publisher=[[Big East Conference]]}} On March 20, in the first round of the [[2026 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2026 NCAA tournament]] against No. 15 seed [[2025–26 Furman Paladins men's basketball team|Furman]], Reed recorded 31 points and 27 rebounds, while shooting 12-of-15 from the field. He became the first player since [[Bill Walton]] in 1972 to have at least 30 points, 20 rebounds and shoot 80% in an NCAA tournament game. He was also the first NCAA tournament player since [[Elvin Hayes]] in 1968 to finish with at least 30 points and 25 rebounds.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/48266296/tarris-reed-31-27-night-helps-uconn-survive-ncaa-tournament |title=Tarris Reed's 31-27 night helps UConn survive in NCAA tournament |publisher=[[ESPN.com]] |date=March 19, 2026| access-date=March 21, 2026}} It marked the 2nd most rebounds in school history in the NCAA tournament, trailing only [[Toby Kimball]] 29 in the 1965 round of 32.{{cite web|url=https://uconnhuskies.com/news/2026/3/21/mens-basketball-reed-jrs-historic-night-leads-2-uconn-past-15-furman|title=Reed Jr.'s Historic Night Leads #2 UConn Past #15 Furman|accessdate=March 23, 2026|date=March 21, 2026|publisher=[[UConn Huskies]]}} He earned Most Outstanding Player for the East All-Region Team.{{cite web|url=https://x.com/MarchMadnessMBB/status/2038410385221419399|title=East All-Region Team|accessdate=March 30, 2026|date=March 29, 2026|publisher=[[National Collegiate Athletic Association]]}} Reed averaged 19.5 points and 13.2 rebounds in UConn's six-game tournament run.{{cite web|url=https://uconnhuskies.com/news/2026/4/6/mens-basketball-huskies-fall-in-national-title-game|title=Huskies Battle To End In Title Game Setback|accessdate=April 14, 2026|date=April 6, 2026|publisher=[[UConn Huskies]]}} Following a loss in the [[2026 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game]], he was named to the all-tournament team.{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/awards/men/ncaa-all-tourney.html|title=Men's NCAA All-Tournament Teams|accessdate=April 13, 2026|publisher=[[Sports
